pr.title: Do not ignore uninhabited types for function-call ABI purposes. (Remove BackendRepr::Uninhabited)
pr.description:
Accepted MCP: https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/832

Fixes #135802

Do not consider the inhabitedness of a type for function call ABI purposes.

* Remove the [`rustc_abi::BackendRepr::Uninhabited`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_abi/enum.BackendRepr.html) variant
  * Instead calculate the `BackendRepr` of uninhabited types "normally" (as though they were not uninhabited "at the top level", but still considering inhabitedness of variants to determine enum layout, etc)
* Add an `uninhabited: bool` field to [`rustc_abi::LayoutData`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_abi/struct.LayoutData.html) so inhabitedness of a `LayoutData` can still be queried when necessary (e.g. when determining if an enum variant needs a tag value allocated to it).

This should not affect type layouts (size/align/field offset); this should only affect function call ABI, and only of uninhabited types.

cc @RalfJung

@rustbot label +A-miri +A-ABI ----- This shouldn't ICE regardless, but whether there is a miscompilation depends on if the original code is sound: CC https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/485
Possible Miscompilation ### Does `#[repr(transparent)]`s ABI-compatility guarantee apply in the prescence of uninhabited 1-ZST fields? A `#[repr(transparent)]` wrapper that contains an uninhabited 1-ZST field gets `Uninhabited` ABI IIUC, which may contradict the guarantees about `#[repr(transparent)]` wrappers being ABI-compatible. Consider `Foo` from above: ```rust type Field = u8; // any non-1ZST probably #[repr(transparent)] struct Foo { _zst: std::convert::Infallible, _field: Field, } ``` If `#[repr(transparent)]`'s ABI-compatility guarantees *do* apply, then the above code should be sound: 1. If a function returns `Foo`, it must diverge (e.g. by panicking). 2. If `Foo` is ABI-compatible with `Field`, then it should be sound to transmute a function pointer to a diverging `fn() -> Foo` into a `fn() -> Field` that also diverges.
rustc_layout(debug) Using `#![feature(rustc_attrs)]` and `#[rustc_layout(debug)]` we see that the ABI it has is ```rs error: layout_of(Foo) = Layout { // snip abi: Uninhabited, // snip } ``` whereas `Field` has ```rs error: layout_of(u8) = Layout { // snip abi: Scalar( Initialized { value: Int( I8, false, ), valid_range: 0..=255, }, ), // snip } ```
### Possible Miscompilation Assuming this is supposed to be sound, then there is an observable miscompilation here too. Where `Field` is returned by invisible reference, `fn(u32) -> Foo` does not return `Foo` by invisible reference, so transmuting `fn(u32) -> Foo` into `fn(u32) -> Field` will pass a different number of arguments. Specifically on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`: If `Field` is returned on the stack, then `fn(..) -> Foo` does not reserve stack space or pass a hidden reference parameter, but `fn(..) -> Field` does. This can be made into an observable miscompilation if the function takes parameters: ([playground link](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=8457797447ef2a581f598b4fe7053f42), IIUC: the invisible reference is being passed, but the callee isn't expecting it, so it thinks it's the first "real" parameter instead (caller: ret by-ref in `rdi`, `x` in `rsi`; callee: ret uninhabited, `x` in `rdi`)).
[^1]: see "Possible Miscompilation" section

processing.reason:
No source-grounded, Miri-defined pair can encode this PR's historical wrong transformation.

1. The only listed pass, GVN, is behavior-preserving in this PR. Pre-fix, every uninhabited layout had `BackendRepr::Uninhabited`, so both the old `BackendRepr::Uninhabited => true` arm and the new `if layout.uninhabited { return true }` check return `true`. Post-fix, `LayoutData::uninhabited` is the same fact previously encoded by that variant (now `backend_repr` is computed normally). Feeding a layout with `uninhabited == true` but a non-uninhabited `backend_repr` to the old arm is not a state the old compiler could produce; it is not a valid input. Thus `type_may_have_niche_of_interest_to_backend` has no concrete input on which the historical and corrected implementations differ.

2. The actual bug fixed by the PR is a function-call ABI lowering bug: an uninhabited `#[repr(transparent)]` return wrapper such as `NoReturn<Large>(Large, Void)` must still use the wrapped type's indirect return ABI and pass a hidden sret pointer. The historical wrong transformation is therefore "omit the return destination / hidden sret argument in call lowering." This is a codegen calling-convention mismatch (caller passes arg in rsi, old callee expects it in rdi). Expressing that mismatch in source requires calling a function through an ABI-incompatible/transmuted signature whose actual layout differs, which is undefined behavior; Miri (required to pass for both candidates) rejects it rather than yielding two defined differing values. Under the fixed modern compiler, both the direct and transmuted calls use the corrected ABI, so any faithful source pair produces the same result.

3. The PR's new tests are an LLVM-IR codegen check and a run-pass UI test that asserts the fixed behavior (`catch_unwind` error plus `correct == true`). The UI test would fail only under the old ABI lowering, not because of a source-to-source rewrite that a fixed compiler can replay. Manufacturing a source pair that manually passes/omits the return slot or manually reads a shifted pointer would not be the historical compiler transformation and would not be defined under Miri.

Therefore the historical semantics and the historically incorrect transformation cannot be reconstructed as two same-signature, ordinary-Rust, Miri-passing functions that yield different defined observable values on the fixed compiler.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, uninhabitedness was encoded directly in `BackendRepr::Uninhabited`; `LayoutData::is_uninhabited()` returned `self.backend_repr.is_uninhabited()`, and GVN matched `BackendRepr::Uninhabited => true` when deciding value validity. Call lowering also treated uninhabited return layouts as ignorable: `ArgAbi` mapped `BackendRepr::Uninhabited` to `PassMode::Ignore`, and `make_return_dest` returned `ReturnDest::Nothing` when there was no `target`. The PR states: "Do not consider the inhabitedness of a type for function call ABI purposes." and "Instead calculate the `BackendRepr` of uninhabited types \"normally\"".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, calls/returns of uninhabited function-call types omitted the return ABI entirely (`PassMode::Ignore`/no return destination). This was wrong for a `#[repr(transparent)]` wrapper such as `enum Void {} #[repr(transparent)] struct NoReturn<T>(T, Void);`: although `NoReturn<Large>` is uninhabited and `T` is returned indirectly, the wrapper's `PassMode` was computed from uninhabitedness rather than from its normal layout, so the caller did not reserve/pass the hidden sret pointer. With arguments this shifted register assignment. The fix computes `BackendRepr` normally, records uninhabitedness separately in `LayoutData::uninhabited`, and still calls `make_return_dest` for an indirect return even when there is no target. GVN correspondingly checks `layout.uninhabited` before matching `backend_repr`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions and function pointers whose return type is uninhabited, especially `#[repr(transparent)]` wrappers containing an uninhabited 1-ZST plus an inhabited, non-ZST field (for example `NoReturn<Large>(Large, Void)` where `Large` is returned indirectly). Include calls with no arguments and with a scalar argument, direct Rust ABI calls, and calls through a transmuted function pointer. The two comparison programs should differ only in the return-type transformation under test: one returns the uninhabited transparent wrapper, the other returns the wrapped inhabited field with otherwise identical arguments and body; the ABI must remain compatible.
analysis.summary: Confirmed bug fix for #135802, not an optimization PR. Removing `BackendRepr::Uninhabited` requires uninhabitedness to be tracked separately, and GVN must consult `LayoutData::uninhabited` rather than infer it from `backend_repr`. The primary ABI fix ensures uninhabited return types are lowered normally so `repr(transparent)` wrappers remain ABI-compatible with their wrapped field, including indirect returns that still need an sret pointer.
analysis.trigger: A function-call ABI is computed for a type known to be uninhabited, particularly a `#[repr(transparent)]` wrapper around an inhabited non-ZST that is returned indirectly; or GVN checks validity of a layout whose `backend_repr` is normal but whose `uninhabited` flag is true.
preconditions: The function return type is uninhabited, or is a `repr(transparent)` wrapper containing an uninhabited field plus an inhabited field.
The return type's normal ABI requires indirect return (`PassMode::Indirect`) for the wrapped inhabited field.
Call lowering may have no `target` destination while `fn_abi.ret` is still indirect, so `make_return_dest` must still add the hidden return pointer to `llargs`.

GVN must not rely on `BackendRepr::Uninhabited`; after the change, uninhabited types can have `Scalar`, `ScalarPair`, or `Memory` backend representations and carry `LayoutData::uninhabited = true` separately.
pitfalls: Do not equate `backend_repr == Memory` or `size == 0` with uninhabitedness; the PR explicitly computes `BackendRepr` normally and records uninhabitedness in a separate field.
Do not treat uninhabited types as `PassMode::Ignore`; `Ignore` is now documented as only for ZSTs, and an uninhabited indirect return still requires an sret pointer.
Do not skip `make_return_dest` merely because there is no branch `target`; the return ABI may still be indirect and the hidden pointer must be appended to `llargs`.

In GVN, failing to check `layout.uninhabited` before `backend_repr` can miss that a value is uninhabited when the normal backend representation is `Scalar` or another inhabited-looking representation.
The ABI change must not be assumed to alter size/alignment/field offsets; the PR says it "should not affect type layouts (size/align/field offset); this should only affect function call ABI".
Do not assume `repr(transparent)` ABI compatibility is automatically preserved for wrappers with uninhabited fields; that is exactly the historical mismatch.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the two new tests as complementary layers. First, a codegen IR test (`tests/codegen/uninhabited-transparent-return-abi.rs`) defines `enum Void {}`, `#[repr(transparent)] struct NoReturn<T>(T, Void)`, and a `Large` type returned indirectly; check that calls with and without an argument still allocate `[24 x i8]`, pass the `sret` pointer in the first argument position, and do not drop the return pointer. Second, a run-pass UI test (`tests/ui/uninhabited/uninhabited-transparent-return-abi.rs`) transmutes `fn(&mut bool) -> NoReturn<Large>` to `fn(&mut bool) -> Large`, calls it under `catch_unwind`, and asserts both that it panics and that the argument was written. For the GVN-specific invariant, exercise a layout whose `backend_repr` is not an uninhabited variant but whose `layout.uninhabited` is true; compare against the same shape with the uninhabited field removed, and inspect debug layout/MIR expectations for the `uninhabited` flag. Update layout-debug stderr baselines for the added `uninhabited` field and for formerly `abi: Uninhabited` dead variants becoming normal `Scalar`/`ScalarPair`/`Memory` layouts with `uninhabited: true`.
